section.title: Keywords
section.p: keywordsdiscoverabilityKeywords improve discoverability in bookstores and reading platforms. They are extracted from the bookmap's <keywords> section and emitted as dc:subject elements in the OPF:
section.codeblock: <keywords> <keyword>artificial intelligence thriller</keyword> <keyword>tech thriller fiction</keyword> <keyword>corporate espionage novel</keyword> </keywords>
section.p: Amazon KDP allows up to seven keyword phrases for search discoverability. Choose phrases that readers would actually search for, not single words.

section.title: BISAC Subject Codes
section.p: BISAC codesBISAC (Book Industry Standards and Communications) codes are the standard subject classification system used by North American publishers and retailers. Amazon uses them for category placement.
BISAC codes can be specified via parameter or bookmap:
section.codeblock: <!-- Via bookmap data elements --> <data name="bisac" value="FIC028080"/><!-- Science Fiction / Hard SF --> <data name="bisac" value="FIC031080"/><!-- Thrillers / Technological --> <data name="bisac" value="FIC028130"/><!-- Science Fiction / Near-Future -->
section.p: When the same code appears in both the parameter and the bookmap, the plugin BISAC deduplicationautomatically deduplicates to avoid emitting the same dc:subject twice. Parameter codes take precedence and are emitted first.
section.note: You can look up BISAC codes at the Book Industry Study Group website. Most retailers expect two to three codes per title. The first code should be the most specific match for your content.

section.title: Description and Blurb
section.p: The first <shortdesc> element in the bookmap's <bookmeta> is extracted as dc:description. This serves as the book blurb in store listings:
section.codeblock: <bookmeta> <shortdesc>When a rogue AI begins rewriting its own code, software architect Elena Vasquez has seventy-two hours to shut it down — or watch it redefine what it means to be alive.</shortdesc> ... </bookmeta>

section.title: Accessibility Metadata
section.p: The plugin automatically generates accessibility metadataEPUB accessibility metadata based on the epub.accessibility parameter. This includes:

ul.li: schema:accessibilityFeature — structural navigation, TOC, reading order, ARIA roles
schema:accessibilityHazard — none (no motion, flashing, or sound hazards)
schema:accessibilityControl — full keyboard and mouse control
schema:accessibilitySummary — conformance statement with the target WCAG level

section.p: No manual configuration is needed. The metadata is derived from the features actually present in the output (e.g., listOfIllustrations is added only when a List of Figures is generated).
